title: A Horizon for the Landfall
premise: Elodie Zhou, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Vantara Syndicate, takes a salvage contract to recover a missing upriver expedition before the seasonal glacier calving closes the route for good. What she finds is a crew alive but changed, guarding a discovery they refuse to name: a drowned valley that remembers its own history in ice. As the Syndicate's collectors close in and the calving season ticks down, Elodie must smuggle the expedition home while deciding whether justice means exposing what they found or burying it. In the end, she pays her debt not with money but with silence traded for leverage, keeps the crew together as an unlikely family, and lets the valley keep its memory — while keeping one fragment of it for herself.
about_author: Wren Villalobos is a former river guide who spent six seasons on glacial waterways before turning to fiction full-time. Their work explores how people build families in transit, and their stories are written mostly in ferry terminals and cheap motels.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Elodie Zhou chases a storm across the flats for hire, radio crackling, while dodging calls from the Vantara Syndicate about her late brother's debt. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: weary competence masking dread — she is good at moving fast because standing still means reckoning.

chapters.title: Terms of Optimism
chapters.summary: A Syndicate broker named Cass offers Elodie a way out: salvage the Meridian expedition, silent since three weeks ago upriver, before calving season opens and closes the route. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the trap disguised as opportunity; she signs because refusing isn't survivable.

chapters.title: Crew of Strangers
chapters.summary: Elodie assembles a skeleton crew: gruff pilot Tomas, superstitious deckhand Imani, and a Syndicate observer named Rell who smiles too easily. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: wary first-day friction; nobody trusts anybody, but the boat needs all hands.

chapters.title: Upriver Silence
chapters.summary: The journey begins through fog and dead radio bands. Imani reads the river like scripture; Rell asks too many questions about the Meridian's cargo manifest. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: creeping unease — the river feels watched, and so does she.

chapters.title: What the Water Gave Back
chapters.summary: They find the Meridian's abandoned supply raft, intact but stripped of instruments, with a logbook ending mid-sentence. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve; Tomas reveals he once lost a crew to this same stretch of river.

chapters.title: The Compass Points Wrong
chapters.summary: Elodie's inherited compass begins drifting toward a side channel no chart acknowledges. Rell insists they stay on route; Elodie follows the needle instead. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: quiet rebellion — trusting her brother's compass over the Syndicate's map.

chapters.title: Voices in the Calving Ice
chapters.summary: At night the crew hears rhythmic cracking from the glacier, almost like speech. Imani refuses to sleep aboard; Rell records everything secretly. POV: Imani. Emotional beat: awe curdling into suspicion — someone aboard is not what they seem.

chapters.title: The Drowned Valley
chapters.summary: Following the compass, they enter a hidden valley where retreating ice has exposed a preserved settlement — whole buildings, artifacts, and the Meridian crew camped among them, alive. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: wonder undercut by alarm; the Meridian leader, Dr. Sefa, greets them like expected guests.

chapters.title: What It Found Before Us
chapters.summary: Sefa explains the valley preserves layered human memory — records, dwellings, a civilization erased from every archive. The Meridian stopped answering radio deliberately. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: conviction versus caution; Sefa believes some things must be protected by forgetting.

chapters.title: Rell's Report
chapters.summary: Elodie discovers Rell transmitting coordinates to the Syndicate. Confrontation on the deck at knife-point ends not in violence but a bargain: Rell admits the Syndicate wants the valley's location for buyers who erase history for profit. POV: Rell. Emotional beat: the observer becomes a defector-in-progress, terrified and honest for the first time.

chapters.title: Debt Collectors on the Water
chapters.summary: A Syndicate gunboat appears downstream, sent to secure the site early. The crews scramble to hide the valley entrance behind a controlled rockslide as the calving season's first collapse thunders nearby. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: desperate teamwork; strangers become a crew under fire.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: Cass boards under a flag of negotiation, offering to forgive Elodie's debt if she hands over Sefa and the valley's core samples. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: temptation laid bare — freedom offered at the cost of everyone she's come to protect.

chapters.title: Memory in a Tin Box
chapters.summary: Imani finds a child's tin box in the settlement containing recordings of ordinary lives — songs, arguments, lullabies. The crew listens together in silence. POV: Imani. Emotional beat: grief and tenderness; the found family forms around shared mourning for people they never met.

chapters.title: A Vote Below Decks
chapters.summary: The combined crews vote: expose the valley to the world and risk the Syndicate seizing it, or seal it and carry only testimony. Sefa argues for silence; a young Meridian researcher argues for truth. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: fracture within the family — justice outside the law has no clean majority.

chapters.title: The Gunboat Moves
chapters.summary: Cass, refused, orders the gunboat to take the valley by force. The crews rig the river narrows with the Meridian's survey charges, gambling that the coming calving will do their work for them. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: cold resolve; Tomas finally faces the river that took his old crew.

chapters.title: Calving Season Opens
chapters.summary: The glacier calves catastrophically. In the chaos, the gunboat is caught in the flood and the valley entrance collapses behind them as the crews run the rapids downstream with the Meridian's evidence hidden in ballast. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: white-knuckle climax — survival bought with permanent loss.

chapters.title: What We Carried Out
chapters.summary: Stranded on a shingle bar, survivors take inventory: most of the crew alive, the tin box saved, the core samples lost to the flood. Cass is pulled from the water, half-drowned, powerless. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: exhausted relief shadowed by what the river kept.

chapters.title: Negotiating with the Drowned
chapters.summary: Elodie offers Cass a trade: her silence about the Syndicate's illegal seizure attempt in exchange for the debt being struck and Rell's reports buried. Cass, facing ruin anyway, agrees. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: justice without law — leverage wielded cleanly for once.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Back in port, the crews decide what to tell authorities: a wreck, a rescue, nothing more. But Sefa privately gives Elodie a copy of one recording from the tin box — a lullaby — saying memory survives by being carried, not archived. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: bittersweet compromise; truth preserved in trust rather than record.

chapters.title: Settling Accounts
chapters.summary: The Syndicate formally releases Elodie's debt; Cass disappears upcountry. Rell, officially a deserter, asks to stay on as crew. Tomas offers his boat as a shared venture. POV: Rell. Emotional beat: cautious belonging — the observer finally has a place to stand.

chapters.title: The Compass Rests
chapters.summary: Elodie visits her brother's grave and tells him the debt is paid, the compass no longer restless. She realizes it was never pointing to the valley — it was pointing her toward people worth keeping. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: release; the instrument of obligation becomes an heirloom of love.

chapters.title: A Horizon for the Landfall
chapters.summary: One year later, the crew runs charter trips on safer waters, a found family with salt in its lungs. On the horizon, the glacier line glitters, keeping its secret. Elodie plays the lullaby once and puts the box away. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: earned peace — home is not a place but the people who ran the river with you.
